checkpoints.prompt: The EC2 compute workload used by the accounting team has a utilization rate of 10% on weekdays and 90% at the end of the month. Choose one approach to consider that will control costs based on operating hours while ensuring sufficient processing capacity at month-end.

choices.text: Measure actual usage at month-end and reassess the normal compute capacity.
choices.explanation: Measuring usage can reduce unnecessary compute capacity outside peak periods.

choices.text: Fix the compute capacity at the month-end peak level for the entire period.
choices.explanation: Because peak capacity is maintained even during low-utilization periods, this does not reassess capacity according to usage.

choices.text: Change to the largest instance without measuring usage.
choices.explanation: Scaling up without measurement makes it impossible to distinguish required performance from excess cost.

choices.text: Keep compute resources running continuously, even when unused, to avoid costs.
choices.explanation: Keeping resources running continuously eliminates the benefit of adjusting compute resources according to usage.

source.label: AWS: Six advantages of cloud computing

checkpoints.title: Provision when needed and reassess the required amount

checkpoints.prompt: An operations engineer found a dependency library on an application running on EC2 that needs to be updated. Choose the one correct party responsible for updating the library.

choices.text: Create a remediation plan as part of the customer-side OS and application updates.
choices.explanation: The customer is responsible for updating the EC2 guest OS and applications installed by the customer.

choices.text: Wait for AWS to update the application's dependency library.
choices.explanation: Responsibility for maintaining dependency libraries does not automatically transfer to AWS.

choices.text: Do not assign an update owner because responsibility is shared.
choices.explanation: Shared responsibility does not mean leaving ownership ambiguous.

choices.text: Ask the physical data center to patch the application.
choices.explanation: Protecting physical facilities and updating applications on EC2 are separate layers.

checkpoints.title: What AWS manages and what you must protect

checkpoints.prompt: A service owner wants the service to continue operating even if EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone stop simultaneously. Choose one architecture that separates the impact of a failure.

choices.text: Place redundant instances in a different AZ.
choices.explanation: Separating instances into a different AZ isolates them from failure domains common to a single AZ.

choices.text: Add more instances in the same AZ.
choices.explanation: Increasing the number of instances does not eliminate the common failure domain of the same AZ.

choices.text: Increase the CPU of the same instance.
choices.explanation: Changing capacity does not isolate an AZ failure.

choices.text: Change only the Region name to another name.
choices.explanation: Changing the name does not change the actual placement or failure domain.

checkpoints.title: Separate failure domains with Regions and AZs

checkpoints.prompt: There is a workload that experiences high load for only one hour each month, with a requirement to continue normal processing even if one AZ stops. Choose two correct starting points for comparison.

choices.text: Compare proposals that increase the required compute capacity only during high-load periods.
choices.explanation: This reflects time-based load variation in capacity planning.

choices.text: Compare the cost of redundancy across AZs, remaining capacity, and the effect of failure isolation.
choices.explanation: For a requirement to continue after an AZ stops, evaluating cost and remaining capacity is necessary.

choices.text: Choose the least expensive single AZ while ignoring the availability requirement.
choices.explanation: Ignoring the requirement in favor of cost alone fails to meet the necessary continuity.

choices.text: Fix the maximum capacity regardless of when the high load occurs.
choices.explanation: Fixing capacity at the peak alone does not allow the load-cost trade-off to be evaluated.

checkpoints.title: Compare load, failures, and costs separately

checkpoints.prompt: A developer needs to run a short transformation only when a file arrives in S3. Choose one way to run it without the team managing the OS.

choices.text: Run Lambda in response to an S3 event
choices.explanation: This enables event-driven processing without managing a server OS.

choices.text: Manually log in to EC2 and run it
choices.explanation: Manual OS operations do not meet the requirements.

choices.text: Use S3 as the execution environment
choices.explanation: S3 is a storage service.

choices.text: Save commands in DynamoDB
choices.explanation: DynamoDB is not a command execution environment.

checkpoints.title: Compute: Who manages the execution environment

checkpoints.prompt: A developer needs multiple processes to read the same image using a key corresponding to its file name. It does not need to be connected as an OS disk. Choose one storage destination that meets the requirements.

choices.text: Store it as an S3 object
choices.explanation: The shared image can be handled using a key.

choices.text: Copy it to each EC2 instance’s EBS
choices.explanation: Managing individual copies will be necessary.

choices.text: Store it only in Lambda’s temporary storage
choices.explanation: This is not a persistent shared storage destination.

choices.text: Always split and store it in RDS
choices.explanation: An RDB is not required for image storage.

checkpoints.title: Storage: Object or attached disk

checkpoints.prompt: A developer searches orders by customer ID and date and joins multiple tables. Transactions are required for simultaneous updates to orders and details. Choose one service to consider first.

choices.text: Consider RDS and verify the relational requirements
choices.explanation: Joins and transactions are the comparison criteria.

choices.text: Always choose DynamoDB without reviewing the requirements
choices.explanation: Choose DynamoDB after verifying the key design.

choices.text: Join using only S3 file names
choices.explanation: S3 does not provide relational joins.

choices.text: Make EBS a shared database directly across multiple AZs
choices.explanation: EBS does not provide database query capabilities.

checkpoints.title: Database: Choose based on the queries

checkpoints.prompt: An e-commerce development team is designing functions to store and transform product images and to let staff search orders. Choose two appropriate ways to divide responsibilities for image storage and order searches, respectively.

choices.text: Assign image storage to S3 objects
choices.explanation: Images can be stored and retrieved by key.

choices.text: Compare order searches against the requirements for RDS or DynamoDB
choices.explanation: Use search characteristics as input for database selection.

choices.text: Consolidate all requirements into manually managed files on EBS
choices.explanation: This ignores the difference between storage formats and queries.

choices.text: Perform image transformation using only database search functionality
choices.explanation: Transformation is a computing responsibility.

checkpoints.title: Combination: Break Requirements Down into Responsibilities

checkpoints.prompt: After an operations administrator signs in to AWS, only a specific S3 operation returns AccessDenied. Select one item to check first.

choices.text: Check the calling principal, operation, target resource, and the policies that apply to them.
choices.explanation: An operation denial after successful authentication calls for isolating authorization.

choices.text: Change the password repeatedly.
choices.explanation: This does not investigate the cause of the denial after successful authentication.

choices.text: Shorten only the DNS TTL.
choices.explanation: DNS does not change IAM permission evaluation.

checkpoints.title: Authentication and Authorization Are Separate Questions

checkpoints.prompt: An operations engineer grants a batch running on AWS permission to write to S3 only during the three hours it is running. Select one way of granting permissions that meets this requirement.

choices.text: The batch principal assumes a trusted role and performs only the required S3 operations using temporary credentials.
choices.explanation: The trust conditions, permissions, and duration can be separated.

choices.text: Give every developer permanent administrator keys.
choices.explanation: These are excessive, long-term shared credentials.

choices.text: Make S3 anonymously writable.
choices.explanation: The principal and target cannot be limited.

checkpoints.title: Principal and role-assumption conditions

checkpoints.prompt: An operations engineer is investigating why an AWS API call from an application using an IAM role was denied. The policy attached to the role allows the call. Choose two other things to check.

choices.text: Check whether an explicit deny applies to the request.
choices.explanation: An applicable explicit deny takes precedence over Allow.

choices.text: Check the ultimately permitted operation, including resource-based policies, applicable conditions, and permissions boundaries.
choices.explanation: The controls are evaluated together.

choices.text: Ignore Deny because Allow is present.
choices.explanation: An explicit deny cannot be ignored.

checkpoints.title: Check explicit Deny as well as Allow

checkpoints.prompt: A developer is restricting the permissions of a Lambda function that reads images from an input prefix in S3 and writes processed results to an output prefix. Choose two appropriate policies.

choices.text: Allow only the required prefixes and actions
choices.explanation: Restrict the target resources and operations to the necessary scope.

choices.text: Use temporary credentials from the execution role
choices.explanation: This avoids distributing long-term keys.

choices.text: Grant administrative permissions for all AWS services
choices.explanation: These are excessive permissions beyond the requirements.

checkpoints.title: Least Privilege and Short-Lived Credentials
Protect data in transit and at rest separately
checkpoints.prompt: A developer stores invoices sent from users’ browsers to an order API in S3. The organization requires HTTPS for communication and SSE-KMS using a specified KMS key for storage. Choose one way to verify both requirements.

choices.text: Separately verify HTTPS across the entire path and the SSE-KMS configuration and KMS key applied to the object in S3.
choices.explanation: This verifies the requirements for encrypting communications and the storage destination’s encryption method and key separately.

choices.text: Verify only that HTTPS is used between the browser and the order API.
choices.explanation: This does not verify the path from the API to S3 or the specified-key requirement for data at rest.

choices.text: Do not verify the KMS key used because S3 default encryption protects new objects.
choices.explanation: S3 default SSE-S3 encryption alone may not satisfy the requirement to use the KMS key specified by the organization.

choices.text: Verify only that the S3 object uses SSE-KMS.
choices.explanation: This does not verify the specified key or HTTPS for the communication path.

learning.reason: Communication and storage are separate boundaries.
learning.concept: Data in transit and at rest

checkpoints.title: Verify the KMS key and access permissions separately
checkpoints.prompt: When an operations engineer tries to read an S3 object encrypted with SSE-KMS from an application, access is denied. Choose one way to isolate the cause.

choices.text: Verify only whether the key ARN is known.
choices.explanation: Identification information is not permission.

choices.text: Grant kms:Decrypt to everyone.
choices.explanation: This grants excessive permissions.

choices.text: Verify the read permission for the S3 object and the decrypt permission allowed by the KMS key policy or IAM policy.
choices.explanation: This verifies the authorization boundaries for the data and the key.

choices.text: Delete and recreate the bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the cause and risks data loss.

learning.reason: This verifies the authorization boundaries for the data and the key.

checkpoints.title: Verify backup success and restorability separately
checkpoints.prompt: A database administrator confirmed that the backup was created successfully. It has not been verified whether order processing can resume within the recovery time objective (RTO). Choose one verification to perform next.

choices.text: Treat the success notification as an audit trail and finish.
choices.explanation: This does not demonstrate restorability.

choices.text: Restore to an isolated destination and record the elapsed time, integrity, and application connectivity.
choices.explanation: This allows comparison of the objective with the measured result.

choices.text: Delete the production data and try a restore.
choices.explanation: This is not a safe test.

choices.text: Change the RTO to match the measured result.
choices.explanation: The measurement must come first.

learning.reason: This allows comparison of the objective with the measured result.

checkpoints.title: Separate secret storage, retrieval, and display
checkpoints.prompt: An operations administrator found a token for an external API used by an order-processing application in the source code and error logs. Choose one action to improve secret management.

choices.text: Make the logs public to everyone for monitoring
choices.explanation: This broadens the scope of the leak.

choices.text: Move it to another source file
choices.explanation: The plaintext problem remains.

choices.text: Make the execution role an administrator
choices.explanation: This does not solve the storage and display problems.

choices.text: Move it to Secrets Manager, restrict who can retrieve it, and remove the value from the logs
choices.explanation: This separates storage, retrieval, and display.

learning.reason: This separates storage, retrieval, and display.

checkpoints.title: IP Is the Destination; the Port Is the Service Entrance
checkpoints.prompt: On the same EC2 instance, SSH succeeds but only HTTPS using port 443 fails. Select one item to check separately first.

choices.text: HTTPS port permission and service listening
choices.explanation: Correct. Even with the same IP, the service entrance is different.

choices.text: Conclude that HTTPS is also working normally based only on the successful SSH connection.
choices.explanation: The port and the higher-level stage are different.

choices.text: Treat the IP address as the port number.
choices.explanation: The IP is the destination; the port is the service entrance.

checkpoints.title: Choose TCP or UDP Based on Where Delivery Responsibility Lies
checkpoints.prompt: The value of old audio that arrives late is low, and the application can be designed to handle loss. Select one correct comparison.

choices.text: Consider UDP and decide at the application layer how to handle any necessary loss and ordering measures.
choices.explanation: Correct. UDP does not guarantee these properties.

choices.text: UDP always guarantees retransmission and ordering.
choices.explanation: These are not standard UDP guarantees.

choices.text: Obtain retransmission guarantees using only the port number.
choices.explanation: The port does not change delivery characteristics.

checkpoints.title: TLS Handles the Communication Channel, While HTTP Handles Application Semantics
checkpoints.prompt: When a user opens a product page in a browser, the TLS handshake succeeds, but HTTP 404 is returned. Choose one place the operations team should investigate first.

choices.text: Routing corresponding to the HTTP URL path or the target product page
choices.explanation: Correct. 404 is an HTTP-stage response.

choices.text: Verification of the TLS certificate name
choices.explanation: TLS has already succeeded.

choices.text: DNS name resolution
choices.explanation: Because the request reached HTTP, DNS did not fail in this observation.

checkpoints.title: Choose the next stage based on evidence, not changes
checkpoints.prompt: DNS and TCP succeeded, but the connection stopped because the TLS certificate hostname did not match. Select one item to check next.

choices.text: The certificate’s SAN (Subject Alternative Name), expiration, and trust chain
choices.explanation: Correct. Check the TLS verification conditions.

choices.text: Only the body of HTTP 404
choices.explanation: The HTTP body has not been retrieved because TLS is not complete.

choices.text: Open all ports
choices.explanation: This does not fix the certificate name mismatch.

checkpoints.title: Until DNS Returns the Record Corresponding to the Domain Name
checkpoints.prompt: A network administrator is investigating why internal.example.com cannot be resolved by an EC2 instance in the VPC. Select one piece of information to check first.

choices.text: Check the association between the querying VPC and the private hosted zone, and check the record name
choices.explanation: This verifies the Resolver's lookup scope and the target name.

choices.text: Reissue the certificate
choices.explanation: This is not directly related to the problem before DNS resolution.

choices.text: Set the TTL to 0
choices.explanation: This does not fix a missing association or record.

choices.text: Unconditionally add the same record to the public zone
choices.explanation: This changes the design boundary for the private name.

learning.reason: This verifies the Resolver's lookup scope and the target name.

checkpoints.title: Choose the DNS record that matches the destination
checkpoints.prompt: A DNS administrator directs example.com, the apex of a Route 53 hosted zone, to a CloudFront distribution. Choose one record configuration to use.

choices.text: CNAME
choices.explanation: You cannot create a CNAME record at the zone apex.

choices.text: MX
choices.explanation: For mail delivery destinations.

choices.text: Alias A or Alias AAAA record
choices.explanation: It can direct traffic to a supported AWS resource by alias.

choices.text: TXT
choices.explanation: It is not used to specify a destination with arbitrary text.

learning.reason: It can direct traffic to a supported AWS resource by alias.

checkpoints.title: TTL is the time a cache can retain a response
checkpoints.prompt: After a DNS administrator switches the destination, some users are still connecting to the old IP address. Choose one reason why shortening the TTL at this point does not make the old response disappear immediately.

choices.text: Route 53 is rejecting the change
choices.explanation: It does not necessarily mean that the change was rejected.

choices.text: The resolver is caching the existing response according to the old TTL
choices.explanation: Existing caches remain until the old TTL expires.

choices.text: A records cannot be changed
choices.explanation: A records can also be changed.

choices.text: The TLS certificate fixes DNS
choices.explanation: TLS and DNS caching are separate.

source.label: Route 53 DNS settings not in effect

learning.reason: Existing caches remain until the old TTL expires.

checkpoints.title: Troubleshoot name resolution and post-connection failures
checkpoints.prompt: An operations engineer confirmed with dig that the order site resolves to the expected IP address. The browser displays a certificate error over the HTTPS connection. Choose one next troubleshooting step.

choices.text: Delete the DNS record
choices.explanation: This breaks name resolution.

choices.text: Shorten the TTL
choices.explanation: This does not fix the existing certificate error.

choices.text: Stop Route 53
choices.explanation: This does not isolate a problem outside DNS.

choices.text: Check the name, validity period, and TLS settings of the certificate presented by the destination
choices.explanation: This verifies the TLS responsibility after DNS succeeds.

learning.reason: This verifies the TLS responsibility after DNS succeeds.

checkpoints.title: Address ranges are determined by prefix length
checkpoints.prompt: Divide 10.0.0.0/24 into /26 subnets. Select one correct statement.

choices.text: Each /26 has 64 addresses and can be placed contiguously
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Each /26 has 256 addresses and overlaps
choices.explanation: /26 has 64 addresses.

choices.text: Changing the prefix length does not change the address range.
choices.explanation: It determines the length of the host portion.

checkpoints.title: Keep subnets within the VPC and avoid overlap
checkpoints.prompt: Divide VPC 10.0.0.0/24 into 10.0.0.0/25 and 10.0.0.128/25. Select one correct verification.

choices.text: Verify that both are within the VPC and do not overlap each other
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Overlap is resolved by route table priority
choices.explanation: Overlapping subnet CIDRs are not allowed.

choices.text: Determine containment by name alone
choices.explanation: Verify using the numeric ranges.

checkpoints.title: Determine capacity after subtracting AWS-reserved IP addresses
checkpoints.prompt: Use an AWS IPv4 /28 subnet. Select one correct estimate of the number of available addresses.

choices.text: Subtract the 5 reserved addresses from 16
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Assign all 16 addresses to EC2
choices.explanation: Reserved IP addresses must be excluded.

choices.text: The number of reserved addresses is determined by the number of route tables
choices.explanation: Reservations are a rule for IPv4 subnets.

checkpoints.title: Verify the conditions for external connectivity
checkpoints.prompt: The EC2 instance has a public IPv4 address, but there is no IGW route in the subnet's route table. Choose one correct judgment.

choices.text: A public IPv4 address alone does not satisfy the conditions for Internet reachability.
choices.explanation: Correct. A route to an IGW is also required.

choices.text: A route can be created using only a NACL.
choices.explanation: A NACL evaluates permissions; it does not create routes.

choices.text: Changing the CIDR eliminates the need for an IGW.
choices.explanation: External reachability requires an appropriate gateway route.

checkpoints.title: Determining the Next Hop from the Destination
checkpoints.prompt: A route table contains 10.0.0.0/8 and 10.1.0.0/16, and the destination is 10.1.2.3. Select one correct conclusion.

choices.text: Choose the /16 route.
choices.explanation: Among the routes that match the destination, the /16 route with the longest prefix is preferred.

choices.text: Choose the /8 route that was registered first.
choices.explanation: The priority of matching routes is not determined by registration order.

choices.text: Send traffic to both the /8 and /16 routes.
choices.explanation: When the destination is included in both ranges, the more specific /16 route is selected.

checkpoints.title: Inbound and Outbound Internet Paths
checkpoints.prompt: Allow only outbound requests from an EC2 instance in a private subnet to an external API. Select the two required components.

choices.text: A default route from the private subnet to the NAT gateway
choices.explanation: In the route table associated with the EC2 subnet, send outbound traffic to the NAT gateway.

choices.text: A route from the public subnet containing the NAT gateway to the internet gateway
choices.explanation: A path from the public NAT gateway to the internet is required.

choices.text: Opening all inbound ports from external sources to the EC2 instance
choices.explanation: It is not necessary to open all ports to external sources to receive responses to connections initiated by the EC2 instance.

choices.text: Attaching an internet gateway directly to an EC2 instance in the private subnet
choices.explanation: An internet gateway is attached to the VPC. In this configuration, outbound traffic from the EC2 instance is sent to the NAT gateway.

checkpoints.title: Difference Between Security Groups and Network ACLs
checkpoints.prompt: For EC2 in a VPC, responses to connections that were allowed to be initiated are permitted without adding reverse-direction allow rules. Select one mechanism that behaves this way.

choices.text: Security group
choices.explanation: Security groups are stateful and allow responses to permitted traffic based on connection state.

choices.text: Network ACL
choices.explanation: Network ACLs evaluate inbound and outbound traffic separately by direction.

choices.text: Route table
choices.explanation: Route tables determine where packets are sent; they do not manage connection state.

checkpoints.title: Troubleshooting private connectivity failures step by step
checkpoints.prompt: The private service name returns the correct IP address, and the destination Security Group already allows the traffic. Select one combination to check next.

choices.text: The source security group's outbound rules, the sender's route, the network ACLs of each subnet, and the return route
choices.explanation: Check not only the destination, but also source authorization and the paths in both directions.

choices.text: Delete the DNS record and add a different name.
choices.explanation: The destination name is already resolving correctly.

choices.text: Allow all traffic using only the destination security group.
choices.explanation: If there is a problem with source authorization or the paths in both directions, this action cannot isolate the cause.

checkpoints.title: Integrate small changes and test immediately
checkpoints.prompt: Immediately after the development team registers a change, the automated tests for the order API fail. Select one action that should be taken as part of the continuous integration process.

choices.text: Stop distribution to the next environment and rerun the same tests after making the fix
choices.explanation: Stop the failure early and validate the fix.

choices.text: Ignore the failure and distribute to production
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the purpose of CI.

choices.text: Delete the tests
choices.explanation: Defects can no longer be detected.

learning.reason: A CI failure stops the subsequent stages.

checkpoints.title: Distinguish continuous delivery from continuous deployment
checkpoints.prompt: The operations team keeps tested changes in a state where they can be released at any time and applies them to production only when the responsible person approves them. Select one option that matches this policy.

choices.text: Continuous deployment
choices.explanation: This method automatically distributes changes to production without human approval.

choices.text: Continuous delivery
choices.explanation: It maintains a state in which changes can be released at any time.

choices.text: Manual rebuild
choices.explanation: This is not a definition of a distributable state.

learning.reason: Delivery means a releasable state.

checkpoints.title: Deliver verified artifacts directly to production
checkpoints.prompt: A release manager deploys the distribution artifact for an order API that passed testing in the verification environment to production. Select one way to use the verified artifact in production.

choices.text: Rebuild in production
choices.explanation: This can create differences from the artifact that was tested.

choices.text: Refer only to the “latest” tag
choices.explanation: The actual artifact cannot be fixed.

choices.text: Distribute the artifact with the same digest or version to the next environment
choices.explanation: This ensures that the artifact tested and the artifact distributed are the same.

learning.reason: Promote the same artifact between environments.

checkpoints.title: Defining conditions for proceeding to the next stage
checkpoints.prompt: The release manager confirmed that the required tests in the validation environment did not meet the passing criteria. Select one action to take next.

choices.text: Stop deployment to the next environment, keep the known-good version, and investigate the cause.
choices.explanation: A quality gate is a stopping condition that prevents artifacts that do not meet the requirements from proceeding to later stages.

choices.text: Continue deployment to production because it is the scheduled time.
choices.explanation: This ignores the unmet conditions.

choices.text: Lower the criteria without keeping an audit trail.
choices.explanation: This is not a reproducible operation.

learning.reason: If the quality gate is not met, stop and investigate.

checkpoints.title: Choosing the Scope Verified by Testing
checkpoints.prompt: A developer observes a failure that occurs only when the order API is connected to an HTTP client, database, and authentication service. Select one type of test that verifies this integration.

choices.text: Integration test
choices.explanation: It verifies connections among multiple components or external boundaries.

choices.text: Unit test
choices.explanation: It targets the local rules of a single function.

choices.text: Static analysis (lint) only
choices.explanation: It does not verify connections at runtime.

choices.text: Screen-image comparison only
choices.explanation: It cannot verify the HTTP, database, and authentication boundaries.

learning.reason: It verifies connections among multiple components or external boundaries.

checkpoints.title: Set inputs, assumptions, and expected values so the test can be reproduced
checkpoints.prompt: A developer regression-tests a calculation in which the tax rate changes based on the effective date. Select two combinations that improve reproducibility.

choices.text: Fix the effective date, tax rate, amount, and expected value
choices.explanation: You can rerun it under the same conditions.

choices.text: Fix the mapping table between the tax rate and expected value for each date and time
choices.explanation: You can reproduce time-dependent branches.

choices.text: Generate the expected value from the execution result
choices.explanation: Errors cannot be detected.

choices.text: Do not save the inputs and expected values when a failure occurs
choices.explanation: Information needed for reproduction is lost.

learning.reason: You can rerun it under the same conditions. You can reproduce time-dependent branches.

checkpoints.title: Use test results as conditions for proceeding to the next step
checkpoints.prompt: A release manager decides whether to deploy to production using quality gates that include required type checks and integration tests. Select two stop conditions.

choices.text: One required integration test fails
choices.explanation: Failure of a required test is a stop condition.

choices.text: The wording of an optional description differs slightly
choices.explanation: This is not an explicitly stated required condition.

choices.text: A required type check fails, and the report is saved
choices.explanation: Stop after confirming the failure and the evidence.

choices.text: Skip artifact identification because all tests passed
choices.explanation: Test success and artifact identity are separate conditions.

learning.reason: Failure of a required test is a stop condition. Stop after confirming the failure and the evidence.

checkpoints.title: Reproduce failures so the same defect can be detected
checkpoints.prompt: A developer confirmed in production a defect that produces an incorrect billing amount at an input boundary value. After fixing it, select one procedure for detecting recurrence of the same defect.

choices.text: Delete the logs and rewrite all the code
choices.explanation: This loses evidence and verifiability.

choices.text: Fix the minimum input and add a regression test after correcting the cause
choices.explanation: You can detect recurrence by reproducing, fixing, and then locking it in with a regression test.

choices.text: Report that it has been fixed without adding a test
choices.explanation: Recurrence under the same conditions cannot be detected.

choices.text: Mock all external boundaries
choices.explanation: This hides actual integration problems.

learning.reason: You can detect recurrence by reproducing, fixing, and then locking it in with a regression test.

checkpoints.prompt: The operations team for the Orders API wants to verify the updated version using only 5% of production requests before switching everyone over. Choose one approach that directly meets this requirement.

choices.text: Bulk task replacement
choices.explanation: Replacing everything at once cannot limit the impact to the initial 5%.

choices.text: Simultaneous switch for all requests
choices.explanation: There is no time to validate the actual traffic on a subset.

choices.text: Canary deployment
choices.explanation: This sends only a portion of the requests to the updated version at first.

choices.text: Database backup
choices.explanation: A backup prepares for restoration; it does not route traffic.

source.label: Amazon ECS deployment controllers and strategies

checkpoints.title: Choose the traffic scope and switching strategy

learning.reason: This sends only a portion of the requests to the updated version at first.
learning.concept: Distinguish replacing tasks from switching where user traffic is sent.

checkpoints.prompt: During a canary release of the Orders API, the updated version’s order completion rate fell below the predefined lower limit. Choose one action the operations team should take first.

choices.text: Immediately send all requests to the updated version
choices.explanation: This expands the impact of the version showing the problem.

choices.text: Remove monitoring of the order completion rate
choices.explanation: Removing monitoring does not resolve failed orders.

choices.text: Stop the previous version
choices.explanation: This removes the environment to which users can be returned and makes recovery more difficult.

choices.text: Stop expanding the switch and confirm the conditions for returning to the previous version
choices.explanation: Because the abort conditions have been met, recovery can begin without expanding the impact.

source.label: Configuring alarms and rollback in AWS CodeDeploy

checkpoints.title: Set the conditions for expanding the release scope and aborting

learning.reason: Because the abort conditions have been met, recovery can begin without expanding the impact.
learning.concept: Decide the monitoring items, observation period, and abort conditions before the release.

checkpoints.prompt: The updated version of the Orders API has a defect. The data format and dependencies have not changed, and the previous version is still running. Choose one action that will restore user operations most quickly.

choices.text: Execute the rollback procedure to the previous version and verify actual order processing
choices.explanation: Because compatibility has been confirmed, switching to the previous version is an available choice.

choices.text: Continue switching to the updated version until the investigation is complete
choices.explanation: This is inappropriate because it expands the impact of the incident.

choices.text: Write back all orders just in case
choices.explanation: There is no indication that the data needs to be written back.

choices.text: Stop only the monitoring notifications
choices.explanation: Stopping notifications does not restore user operations.

source.label: Rollback and redeployment in AWS CodeDeploy

checkpoints.title: Choose rollback to the previous version and application of the fixed version

learning.reason: Because compatibility has been confirmed, switching to the previous version is an available choice.
learning.concept: Check compatibility with the data and dependencies before applying the previous version.

checkpoints.prompt: With the old and new order APIs running concurrently, you are changing the column that stores delivery destinations. Select two actions that operations personnel should take for a safe migration and recovery.

choices.text: Delete the old column while the previous version is still running
choices.explanation: If the previous version uses that column, processing will fail.

choices.text: Do not record database changes
choices.explanation: A change history is needed to investigate incidents and decide how to restore the system.

choices.text: Add the new column and test the old and new read and write operations in advance
choices.explanation: This verifies that the previous and updated versions can use the same database.

choices.text: Restore from a backup to a separate environment and try to verify the order data
choices.explanation: This verifies the data and procedures needed after restoration.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Database Schema Changes

checkpoints.title: Create a data structure usable by both old and new applications

learning.reason: This verifies that the previous and updated versions can use the same database. This verifies the data and procedures needed after restoration.
learning.concept: Add and migrate first, then remove the old structure after the previous version is no longer needed.

checkpoints.title: Find anomalies and trace a single request
checkpoints.prompt: An operations person for the Orders API investigates, for one slow request, whether the Inventory Service or the Payment Service took more time. Choose the most appropriate data to use.

choices.text: The Orders API’s average response time over one hour
choices.explanation: An aggregate value cannot show how much time each service took for one specific request.

choices.text: The target request’s trace and the time taken by each call
choices.explanation: A trace records the time for each processing step along the path of one request.

choices.text: One log line from when the Orders API started
choices.explanation: A startup record does not show the processing time for the target request.

choices.text: The name of the Orders API’s SLO
choices.explanation: The SLO name alone cannot be used to inspect individual calls.

learning.reason: A trace records the time for each processing step along the path of one request.
learning.concept: Use metrics to narrow the scope of an anomaly.

checkpoints.title: Observe response time, errors, load, and capacity
checkpoints.prompt: Users of the Orders API are waiting longer, and server processing queues are also growing. Choose two aspects the operator should examine when investigating response time and spare processing capacity.

choices.text: Saturation
choices.explanation: A growing queue may indicate that processing capacity is nearing its limit.

choices.text: Traffic volume
choices.explanation: This shows the request volume, but how much spare processing capacity remains must be investigated separately.

choices.text: Error rate
choices.explanation: The proportion of failed processing and the time until a response are separate metrics.

choices.text: Response time
choices.explanation: This measures how long users waited for a response.

learning.reason: A growing queue may indicate that processing capacity is nearing its limit. The time users waited for a response can be measured.
learning.concept: Measure the impact on users with response time and errors.

checkpoints.title: Define quality metrics and objectives
checkpoints.prompt: The operations team for the order API uses CloudWatch to determine success or failure for each request and sets an SLO targeting a success rate of at least 99.9%. Select two items needed to determine the success rate and whether the objective has been met.

choices.text: The operations included in the aggregation and which responses count as successful
choices.explanation: When the scope and success criteria are defined, other team members can calculate the success rate in the same way.

choices.text: The target value of 99.9% and the aggregation period for counting the in-scope requests.
choices.explanation: For a request-level SLO, verify which period's requests to aggregate and which target value the resulting percentage must meet.

choices.text: Only the name of the SLO to display
choices.explanation: Choosing a name does not define how quality is measured or the conditions for achieving the objective.

choices.text: Only the alert notification destination
choices.explanation: The notification destination is not a condition needed to calculate achievement.

learning.reason: When the scope and success criteria are defined, other team members can calculate the success rate in the same way. Evaluating the objective requires both the percentage and the period over which the in-scope requests are aggregated.
learning.concept: An SLI is the value being measured, while an SLO is the objective to achieve for that value.

checkpoints.title: Formulate hypotheses about causes and measure the effectiveness of countermeasures
checkpoints.prompt: After an operations engineer deploys the order API to production, the response time increases. Select the most appropriate method for determining whether this deployment caused the issue.

choices.text: Confirm the cause as soon as the response becomes slower immediately after the deployment
choices.explanation: The request volume or the state of dependencies may also have changed during the same period.

choices.text: Remove the latency metric and restore the monitoring dashboard to normal
choices.explanation: Changing the display does not shorten the user's wait time.

choices.text: Compare before and after the change under the same load and aggregation conditions, and also check the logs and traces
choices.explanation: Keeping the comparison conditions consistent helps isolate the impact of the change from other factors.

choices.text: Change the response-time objective based on a single metric
choices.explanation: Changing the objective before investigating how long the condition will persist does not reveal the cause.

learning.reason: Keeping the comparison conditions consistent helps isolate the impact of the change from other factors.
learning.concept: Test hypotheses within a narrowly defined scope.
